chapters.title: Household Document Readiness
chapters.summary: Local routines for keeping identity, insurance, and household records usable during evacuation, outage, or paperwork-heavy recovery.

sections.heading: Grab-First Record Pouch
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Choose one small set of records you would actually grab under pressure.

- Keep the pouch limited to identity, insurance, medical, and contact essentials.
- Make sure every document inside answers a real post-evacuation question.
- Store it where adults in the household can name the location without guessing.
- Review it after every address, insurance, or household-member change.

A smaller pouch that stays current is better than a larger binder nobody can carry fast.

sections.heading: Insurance And Home Photo Sweep
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Treat home-inventory photos like maintenance, not a once-ever project.

- Photograph rooms, major equipment, and high-value items from a repeatable angle.
- Keep dates and broad item descriptions consistent so later comparison is easier.
- Capture updates after large purchases, remodels, or moves.
- Store the newest set where you can retrieve it without hunting through unrelated images.

Short regular sweeps are easier to trust than one giant archive from years ago.

sections.heading: Household Identity And Contact Redundancy
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Do not make one phone the single point of failure for household records.

- Keep at least one offline contact list that does not depend on battery or cellular service.
- Make sure key policy numbers and emergency contacts appear in more than one place.
- Review who in the household can unlock or locate the critical document set.
- Remove stale cards, outdated contacts, and expired IDs before they create confusion.

Redundancy is less about more storage and more about fewer surprises when power, signal, or time runs short.
